elements.element: Customer owns Deliverables and work product created for Customer.
elements.evidence: Neither the retained text nor the inserted clause states that the Issuer owns the Receivable Files, Monthly Investor Reports or other work product; the insertion is a licence grant only ("The Servicer grants the Issuer a perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free license..."), and Section 3.10(b) speaks only of custody "for the benefit of the Issuer and the Indenture Trustee".

elements.element: Vendor assigns the Deliverables and work product to Customer.
elements.evidence: No assignment language appears anywhere in the rendered text; the only operative transfer is a licence.

elements.element: Vendor retains its pre-existing intellectual property.
elements.evidence: Retained Section 7.5(b): "The Servicer will not be obligated to provide, license or assign its processes, procedures, models, servicing software or other applications to any Successor Servicer or any third party"; the new grant is confined to files, reports, records and materials and does not reach those assets.

elements.element: Customer's licence to Vendor IP embedded in Deliverables is perpetual.
elements.evidence: "perpetual ... license to use, modify and sublicense for its business the Receivable Files, the Monthly Investor Reports and the other reports, records and materials delivered or made available to the Issuer" — the grant runs to the delivered materials, including any Servicer IP embedded in them.

elements.element: Customer's licence to embedded Vendor IP is irrevocable.
Customer's licence to embedded Vendor IP is royalty-free.
elements.evidence: "royalty-free license to use, modify and sublicense for its business".

elements.element: Customer retains all rights in Customer Data.
elements.evidence: No sentence states that the Issuer retains all right, title and interest in the Receivable Files or other Issuer data; custody "for the benefit of the Issuer and the Indenture Trustee" is a bailment concept, not a retention-of-rights statement.

elements.element: Any Vendor licence in Customer Data is limited to processing it solely to provide the Services.
elements.evidence: Inserted: "The Servicer may process the Receivable Files and all other data belonging to, supplied by or processed for the Issuer solely to provide the servicing and custodial services under this Agreement." The trigger covers every category of Issuer data, not selected types.

elements.element: The parties do not jointly own intellectual property.
elements.evidence: No joint-ownership language exists in the cited or rendered text, and the edit creates none; the condition the element guards against does not arise.

elements.element: Vendor may retain ownership of generic tools and know-how.
elements.evidence: Retained Section 7.5(b) preserves the Servicer's "processes, procedures, models, servicing software or other applications"; the redline leaves that sentence intact and the new licence does not sweep it in.

elements.element: Customer's licence to Deliverables is perpetual.
elements.evidence: "The Servicer grants the Issuer a perpetual ... license".

elements.element: Customer's licence to Deliverables is irrevocable.
Customer's licence to Deliverables is worldwide.
Customer's licence to Deliverables is royalty-free.
elements.evidence: "royalty-free license to use, modify and sublicense".

elements.element: Customer may use and modify Deliverables for its business.
elements.evidence: "license to use, modify and sublicense for its business the Receivable Files, the Monthly Investor Reports and the other reports, records and materials delivered or made available to the Issuer under this Agreement".

elements.element: Customer may sublicense Deliverables for its business.
elements.evidence: "use, modify and sublicense for its business" — sublicensing is expressly within the same business-purpose grant.

elements.element: Any Vendor licence in Customer Data is limited to processing it solely to provide the Services.
elements.evidence: "The Servicer may process the Receivable Files and all other data belonging to, supplied by or processed for the Issuer solely to provide the servicing and custodial services under this Agreement." No resale, independent-exploitation or "purposes contemplated by this Agreement" tail remains.

reasons: The finding is position-complete at the fallback: every fallback element is met in operative language — a perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free licence to use, modify and sublicense the delivered files, reports, records and materials for the Issuer's business, plus a solely-to-provide-the-services limit on Servicer processing that covers all data belonging to, supplied by or processed for the Issuer.

Preferred is not complete: there is no statement that the Issuer owns the Receivable Files, reports and other work product, no Servicer assignment of them, and no sentence that the Issuer retains all rights in its data. If the drafter wants the preferred level, add (i) "The Issuer owns all right, title and interest in the Receivable Files, Monthly Investor Reports and other materials created for the Issuer, and the Servicer assigns all such rights to the Issuer," and (ii) "The Issuer retains all right, title and interest in all data belonging to, supplied by or processed for it."

Minimality holds: a single concise insertion for an otherwise missing clause, no deletions, no survival tail, no expense or damages language, no notwithstanding override of Section 7.5(b), and no requirement outside the fallback checklist. The data-processing sentence is required by the eighth fallback element, so it is not an extra.

Intent is preserved: the transition, expense, custody and Indenture-compliance mechanics survive unchanged, the Servicer's retained processes/models/software carve-out is untouched and does not contradict the new grant (which is limited to delivered files, reports and materials), and no defined term or cross-reference is left dangling.

Drafting nit only (not a defect): the inserted clause is untitled by section number — give it a subsection designation (e.g., "(d) License of Deliverables; Use of Issuer Data") so the Section 7.5 lettering remains sequential.
